confirmed.title: Against an Active Caterpie, EndTurn is never priced, so the searcher's own reading still counts the Energy it is about to waste
confirmed.scenario: Lucario list is player 0, to move on turn 4. Its Active is Riolu with no Energy, Mega Lucario ex is in the deck, this turn's [F] is unused and the next one is [F]. The Sceptile list is player 1, with Active Caterpie and its deck Unknown in the search state. Caterpie's Quick Growth trips the guard at observation.rs:370-386, so hidden_continuation_reason returns "automatic next-turn ability searches an unknown deck" for every EndTurn, including the forced one after an attack. expectiminimax_player.rs:441 then scores the state before EndTurn. After a voluntary EndTurn, that state has player 0 to move, no attack used and no end marker, so owner_turn_is_over is false and `running` is true. ThroughNextTurn therefore counts current [F] + next [F], and Riolu reads 2 of 2 for Fighting Pulse (1.0). In every other matchup the EndTurn leaf is taken after the turn has passed and reads next only (0.5). So 'EndTurn without attaching' gets the same Active score as 'attach to Riolu, then EndTurn': the 250 (0.5 x 500) that 0adfeb7 calls 'really lost' is never charged. The clock doesn't move on this board, because Fighting Fist (missing 0) is the threat either way. The same happens to an unused Ice Maker or Roar in Unison. Roar even scores higher left unused: its 2 [D] are counted without its 30 damage. No leaf of the searcher's search crosses its EndTurn while Caterpie is the opposing Active.
confirmed.why: This is the one place in the yardstick where amendment 5's premise fails. The premise is that a source left unused at the end of the turn is lost and the search charges for it. It applies in the Sceptile list's 7 matchups, on the opponent's turns while Sceptile's Active is Caterpie. That's the usual opening: 2 of the list's 3 Basics are Caterpie, and it evolves at the end of the next turn. On the boards I checked it doesn't change the move. Attaching still gains pokemon_value (here +60), and at the root Attach sorts after EndTurn in canonical_actions, so it wins exact ties. It would only bite with a source that has a cost (Roar in Unison on a Hydreigon that isn't attacking). I couldn't make that come up against a 40-HP Caterpie, because Roar plus the attach always pays Hyper Ray for the knockout. It belongs in the known limits more than in a fix before the table.

confirmed.title: An end-of-turn knockout leaves the promotion pending at the leaf, so the replacement is read as 'no Active' instead of projected
confirmed.scenario: Hydreigon list is player 0, to move: Mega Absol ex Active with [D][D] and Deceptive Needle. Suicune list is player 1: Frigibax Active on 10 HP (60 HP card), Chien-Pao ex (no Energy) and Baxcalibur on the Bench, [W] showing next. Line X is Darkness Claw. Frigibax is knocked out by the attack, and player 1's Promote frame is resolved in the search at the same depth (min). EndTurn follows, and the leaf reads the replacement at its next attack: this turn's [W] plus Ice Maker's [W]. For Chien-Pao ex, Icicle is paid: online 1.0 against k's 0 (-500 for player 0), and the threat is Icicle missing 0 against 1 (-100). For Baxcalibur, Buster Tail reads 2 of 3 (-333). Buster Tail (90, missing 1) then displaces Icicle (20, missing 1) as the threat, so the clock drops from about 10 turns to about 3 (-700). Line Y is EndTurn. The Needle's 10 knocks Frigibax out inside on_end_turn. trigger_promotion_or_declare_winner inserts the Promote frame at index 0 (state/mod.rs:1428), then advance_turn pushes player 1's DrawCard on top (state/mod.rs:1211). The promotion check at expectiminimax_player.rs:723 only looks at the top frame, so the Unknown-hand guard at 773 scores the leaf with player 1's Active slot empty. The online score is 0 (value_functions.rs:2026), and the threat is scanned from the Bench unprojected (value_functions.rs:891 projects slot 0 only). The kpr change alone therefore adds about 600 to Y's lead over X (Chien-Pao ex promoted) or about 1,000 (Baxcalibur promoted, which the min would likely pick). With Hydreigon as the replacement it adds 500 + 300. In reality, after Y, player 1 promotes the same Pokémon and it reads the same.
confirmed.why: Amendment 5 says neither reading steps inside the search. At an end-of-turn knockout, though, the knocked-out side's reading drops to 'no Active' on lines where the end of turn does the knockout, but becomes the projected replacement on lines where an attack does. Five of the eight lists do damage at the end of the searcher's turn: Deceptive Needle (Hydreigon, Weezing), poison (Terminating Tail, Boiler Smog), burn (Mega Burning, Boiler Smog) and Bad Dreams (Altaria). So this comes up whenever an Active is low. k has the same pending-promotion leaf, but there an unpowered replacement reads about 0 anyway. kpr widens the gap from about 0 to 500 x its projected readiness plus 100 per clock turn. The bias favors letting the end of turn take the knockout, which is usually also right (no attack Energy spent), and k already leans that way on this board (an empty Active has 0 safety). So I expect a small table effect. It will override any real edge of the attack line smaller than 600-1,000, such as the Needle's 10 on the replacement or a Bench hit like Shadow Bullet's 20. The same pending-promotion leaf also appears when an attack's own follow-up choice (Reverse Thrust's switch) is cut off at depth 0.

**Why it is only minor:**

- **Same direction as k.** k already favours the pending-promotion leaf, because an empty Active scores 0 safety against the replacement's HP divided by its KO points (about 30–150). k also already has the full 500 gap whenever the likely replacement already holds Energy. kpr only widens that gap for unpowered or part-powered replacements.
- **No decision change on the finding's own board.** Darkness Claw against EndTurn: both k and kpr choose EndTurn. The real cost is just the Needle's 10 on the replacement.
- **The favoured line is often the right one.** In several cases the end-of-turn knockout really is the better play:
  - Mega Burning discards Fire Energy.
  - Hyper Ray discards all Energy.
  - Dynamite Punch does 20 to itself.
  - Blaziken's better line is Tongue Whip on the Bench and letting the burn knock the Active out.
  - Altaria's attack line gains nothing over Bad Dreams.
- **Flips need a narrow window.** kpr only chooses differently from k when the attack line's real edge sits between k's safety bias (about 100) and kpr's widened gap (about 600–1,100). Concrete cases I found:
  - The Needle's 10 turns the replacement into a one-hit knockout for Claw or Dark Prism (clock one turn faster, about 100).
  - Shadow Bullet's 20 on the Bench (Weezing list).
  - Weezing list's single Darkrai ex holding the Needle: Nightmare Aura knocks the Active out mid-turn, then Dark Prism hits the replacement. kpr may skip that free 80–90 damage in favour of letting the Needle take the knockout.
- **Rare preconditions.** Every flip needs the opponent's Active to start the searcher's turn at exactly 10 HP or less (Needle), 20 or less (burn, Bad Dreams) or 30 or less (Boiler Smog), with the end-of-turn source live. That is a small share of turns in the Hydreigon and Weezing lists, and the cost is tens of HP per flip. A table effect below noise is the likely outcome.

The Reverse Thrust depth-0 variant exists: Team Rocket's Koffing is in the Weezing list. But it also needs Reverse Thrust's 10 damage to knock the Active out, and it ends up in the same small bias. So this is a correct, specific finding with a marginal effect on kpr's play and on the table.

findings.title: No test builds the real turn-start leaf (the opponent's DrawCard frame on the stack), so the continuity amendment 5 relies on is unpinned: a 'DrawCard ends the turn' mutation survives
findings.scenario: Every line that ends the searcher's turn, attacks included, is scored at the opponent's turn start with (opp, [DrawCard{1}]) on top of the stack (advance_turn -> queue_draw_action, state/mod.rs:1114). The opponent's zone has also rotated: `current` is the old `next`, and `next` is None, because the observation clears the opponent's energy_types (observation.rs:60) and rotate_energy_zone then rolls nothing. The one test of this boundary, the_opponents_reading_is_the_same_either_side_of_its_turn_start (line 3385), builds `after` with an empty stack. Its board can't tell `current` from nothing anyway: Chien-Pao ex with a benched Baxcalibur reads Icicle paid, clock 10, from Ice Maker alone. Mutation, not in mutate.py: add `| SimpleAction::DrawCard { .. }` to the markers at lines 2066-2072, or make line 2065 `choices.len() == 1`. None of the 23 kpr feature tests puts a non-marker frame on the stack while expecting 'running'. The Hyper Ray get_player test can't see it either: the opponent's Suicune ex already holds [W][W], so Crystal Waltz is paid either way and the Bulbasaur is benched. In the Darkness Claw test the claw wins outright. So the mutant passes everything. Board where it matters: the opponent (Hydreigon list) has Mega Absol ex Active with no Energy and [D] next. The code as it stands reads it the same before and after the rotation: 1 of 2, Darkness Claw missing 1. The mutant, at the turn-start leaf, reads the turn as over, looks at turn+2's `next` (None) and gives 0 of 2, missing 2.
findings.why_it_matters: The mutant puts back a step at every turn end, in the direction opposite to the one 0adfeb7 and 1981bb4 removed: about +350 for the searcher (+250 score, +100 clock) on every line that ends its turn, compared with lines cut mid-turn, whenever the opponent's Active is short and holds no Energy Ability. That covers most boards in all 28 pairings. The code is right today, but nothing would catch a refactor of the 'forced single choice' marker.

checked_and_correct: Energy Zone timing: the zone rotates only for the incoming player at advance_turn (state/mod.rs:1212). In the blind search the opponent's new `next` is None (energy_types cleared at observation.rs:60, not restored by search_state). ThroughNextTurn and NextAttack read the same Energy on both sides of the opponent's rotation and of the searcher's EndTurn. Turn 1 and 2 follow state/mod.rs:767-772.
ability_used is reset for both players in end_turn_maintenance at every advance_turn, so the opponent's 'this turn' Abilities at its turn-start leaf equal its 'next turn' Abilities before it.

For EndTurn, hidden_continuation_reason can only fire for setup (turn 0, where nothing is projected), the Caterpie/StartTurnRandomPokemonToHand guard, or an empty private frame on top. EndTurn has no effect text, so the thread-local public-pricing flag doesn't change end_turn_scored_before_it, and tests run outside with_public_pricing match in-game behavior.

end_turn_scored_before_it is only evaluated when the owner is to move (short-circuit), so its `next = 1 - current_player` is the opponent. In the yardstick decks only Caterpie trips the guard (no StartTurnRandomPokemonToHand holder).

In the yardstick decks, the only Energy Abilities are Roar in Unison and Ice Maker. Nightmare Aura (Darkrai ex) is passive damage, not a source. Flame Patch (Blaziken list) is an Item in a hidden hand, so leaving it out is consistent with 'public sources only'.

The engine gates Roar and Ice Maker the same way the projection does: the zone-to-Active turn block via attach_energy_from_zone and can_attach_energy_from_zone, ability_used, and a [W] Active for Ice Maker (move_generation_abilities.rs:112-121, 361-371).

energy_missing and get_effective_attached_energy work on the passed PlayedCard, so the projected copy is priced correctly. The damage estimator reads the slot's own Energy for Fighting Pulse (ExtraDamageIfExtraEnergy) and includes no this-turn bonuses (Korrina, Fighting Coach, Arena of Antiquity, Training Area). So there's no this-turn bonus combined with next-turn Energy.

1981bb4's claim that a lower-ratio yardstick switch needs mixed-type costs holds for the yardstick decks, including [DDC] (Hoopa ex, Darkrai ex) and [CCC] (Darkrai): with a single Energy type, missing counts only tie at 0.

Wiring: the KPR arm is the KP arm with the kpr value function. 'kpr' parses before 'kp'. The value function's arguments (public, no value term, clock, effect-aware, not reserve-aware) match k's. EvalFeatures::KPR has kq's and kd's features off. legality_scan pilots both sides through parse_player_code.
The engine diff from 53638a7 (identity replay) to HEAD is confined to kpr code in value_functions.rs, as 14c7d9b says.

Searches rooted in the opponent's turn (the searcher promoting after a knockout) cross the opponent's EndTurn and the searcher's turn start. Every Promote child crosses the same boundaries at the same depth, so neither reading steps between the root's choices. The searcher's in-search `next` is exact for the one-type yardstick decks.

Amendment 6's own reading in Caterpie positions is the same at mid-turn cuts, at the unpriced EndTurn leaf and at the post-attack leaf (all 'over', next turn's sources only), so 0adfeb7's +350 step doesn't return there.
